2026-09-09.title: #cD542: Snabbit’s 15-Minute Beauty Fix
2026-09-09.articleText:
How long does it take for you to get a basic threading or quick hair-styling done before a last-minute office presentation or an evening event? Traditionally, it meant calling a local salon hours in advance, travelling through traffic, or waiting for a scheduled home-salon technician to arrive in a 2-hour delivery window. Bengaluru-based startup Snabbit is upending this status quo by taking the "instant" ethos of quick-commerce and applying it directly to personal grooming.

• Snabbit initially built its core engine around hyper-local, on-demand domestic home services, aggregating and formalising household cleaning, chores, and maintenance.

• By focusing on ultra-dense neighborhood micro-markets, Snabbit achieved sub-15-minute fulfillment times for daily household chores.

• Having raised over US$112 million, including a massive Series D round, the company is now executing a natural category expansion- instant, salon-at-home services.

The business logic behind Snabbit’s foray into beauty is rooted in customer overlap and purchase frequency.

• While traditional at-home beauty models rely on planned, high-ticket packages with long appointment wait times, Snabbit targets high-frequency, low-ticket daily beauty needs such as threading, waxing, quick facials, and saree draping

• Its strategy hinges on supply-side innovation- beauty professionals are cross-trained into multi-skilled service providers capable of handling multiple tasks in a single session.

• Combined with lightweight, single-use monodose kits from premium brands like O3+ and Rica, workers can travel light and complete jobs rapidly within a tight geographic radius.

Operating on a unit-pricing revenue model starting as low as Rs.49 with no minimum order requirements, Snabbit extracts platform commission while maximizing the daily utilization rates of its all-women service workforce. This instant-fulfillment beauty vertical deepens platform stickiness, converting occasional app users into daily active consumers who rely on Snabbit for both house cleaning and quick personal grooming.

For business, marketing, and operations graduates, the rise of instant home services creates entry-level roles across vendor acquisition, micro-market operations, supply chain management, and growth marketing. Building density in neighborhood clusters demands field-level execution, customer engagement, and tactical partner management.

2026-09-10.title: #cD536: Bajaj’s FMEG Shift
2026-09-10.articleText:
When Kamalnayan Bajaj acquired Radio Lamp Works in 1938 to distribute Italian radio lamps, he hit a wartime snag. World War II disrupted imports, forcing the company to pivot from trading to manufacturing in Shikohabad. By 1960, that single factory evolved into Bajaj Electricals.

For decades, the company operated on a distinct thesis- act as a national marketing umbrella for over 100 small-scale manufacturers who had craft, but lacked capital and distribution muscle.  

• While competitors built heavy factories, Bajaj chose an asset-light model, relying on third-party sourcing for up to 80% of its volume.  
• Fast-forward to its centenary year, and the fast-moving electrical goods (FMEG) landscape has shifted dramatically.  
• Aggressive competitors like Havells, Crompton Greaves, Wipro Consumer Care, and Stovekraft built extensive in-house manufacturing infrastructure exceeding 70% of their total output to maintain tight quality control, higher gross margins, and rapid product innovation.
Recognizing this growth gap, Chairman Shekhar Bajaj orchestrated a structural overhaul to outpace industry growth by FY27.  

• The company demerged its capital-intensive Engineering, Procurement, and Construction (EPC) business into an independent listed entity named Bajel Projects, insulating its consumer segment from heavy working-capital drag.  
• Now operating as a pure-play consumer durables enterprise, Bajaj Electricals is redirecting capital toward research, design, and market expansion.  
• Its comprehensive multi-brand portfolio- encompassing Bajaj, Morphy Richards, Nirlep, and premium fan label Nex - is being upgraded through targeted R&D and artificial intelligence tools to shorten product development timelines and launch higher-margin variants directly through its nationwide traditional and quick-commerce trade networks.
For management graduates, this corporate turnaround offers practical insights into how legacy business houses re-engineer distribution channels and product portfolios under intense market pressure.  

• Sustainable growth in the FMEG space depends heavily on frontline commercial execution.  
• Entry-level opportunities in Sales, Customer Engagement, and Client-facing Channel Management remain vital entry points.  
• Management trainees managing distributor networks, designing trade promotional schemes, and securing retail shelf placement gain direct exposure to real-world commercial operations.  
• It equips them with key competencies for long-term strategic leadership roles in scaling consumer durables brands across rapidly expanding regional Indian consumer markets.

2026-09-11.title: #cD512: SMFG’s Strategic NBFC Expansion
2026-09-11.articleText:
When a global financial heavyweight doubles down on a developing market, it signals far more than standard capital allocation; it underlines structural faith in grassroots economic mobility. Japanese banking titan Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group (SMFG) recently executed a rights issue infusing Rs. 1,075 crore into its Indian non-banking financial company (NBFC) arm, SMFG India Credit.

This substantial equity boost follows significant operational momentum, with assets under management rising 21% year-on-year to Rs.64,100 crore and disbursements expanding 29% to Rs.39,500 crore. The strategic intent is clear: bolstering capital adequacy to fund the next phase of growth across retail, micro, small, and medium enterprise (MSME) lending in India’s vibrant semi-urban and rural markets. This capital injection reinforces Japanese financial commitment to India’s long-term credit story, cementing its competitive position.

Formerly known as Fullerton India Credit, the entity has evolved into a key vehicle for expanding formal credit across historically unserved segments. With a footprint spanning over 670 towns and 70,000 villages through more than 1,000 branches and 22,500 employees, scaling up requires balancing aggressive distribution with prudent risk management.

The fresh infusion is earmarked for expanding loan portfolios across SME financing, two-wheeler loans, home loans, and rural livelihood loans, while accelerating digital transformation. Additionally, strengthening governance and regulatory compliance ensures that risk frameworks keep pace with rapid book growth. By pairing new-age digital onboarding tools with a massive ground workforce, the company effectively bridges the trust gap for borrowers lacking conventional credit histories.This hybrid model - combining physical branch touchpoints with digital payment rails and data-driven underwriting enables global capital to power local entrepreneurship.

This nationwide expansion creates dynamic entry-level career pathways for management graduates across tier-2 and tier-3 cities. Frontline business development, merchant acquisition, client relationship management, and customer engagement serve as the primary growth engines in retail finance.

Entry-level candidates entering NBFCs can target realistic roles in credit underwriting, branch operations, partner acquisition, and digital product adoption in addition to back-office risk modelling and financial analysis roles.

Achieving sustained success in this evolving domain requires a strong blend of digital fluency and market empathy- understanding both algorithmic credit risk scores and the practical daily cash flow dynamics of local business owners.
